examples.ko: 카페인을 과다하게 마시면 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: If you drink too much caffeine, you cannot sleep.
Costs are excessive this month, so I am worried.

examples.ko: 정보가 과다한 시대에는 필요한 것만 골라야 해요.
examples.en: In an age of information overload, you have to pick only what you need.

examples.ko: 설탕이 과다한 음료는 몸에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Drinks with too much sugar are bad for you.
The workload was excessive, so I worked until late at night.
Excessive greed actually ruins things.

explain: '너무 많다'를 공식적으로 말할 때 써요. 음식·비용·정보·업무처럼 양을 말하고, '과다하게', '과다한' 형태로 자주 나와요. 모자랄 때는 '부족하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The formal way to say 'too much'. It is used for amounts of food, cost, information or work, usually as '과다하게' or '과다한'. When there is too little, say '부족하다'.

examples.en: That company sells off its old building.
I decided to sell the land to pay off my debt.

examples.ko: 주식을 매각하면 세금을 내야 할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you sell your shares, you may have to pay tax.

examples.ko: 가게를 다른 사람에게 매각하고 시골로 이사 갔어요.
examples.en: They sold the shop to someone else and moved to the countryside.

examples.ko: 집을 매각할 때는 중개인이 많이 도와줘요.
examples.en: A broker helps a lot when you sell a house.
They explained to the staff why they wanted to sell the factory.

explain: '팔다'와 같지만 격식 있고 규모가 큰 재산에 써요. 가게에서 물건 하나를 팔 때는 '매각하다'라고 하지 않아요. 반대는 '매입하다'예요.
explain_en: Same idea as 팔다 but formal and for large assets. You would not say 매각하다 for selling a single item in a shop. The opposite is 매입하다 (to buy in).

en: be sluggish; be in a slump; perform poorly

examples.en: Sales have been sluggish lately.
That player's recent results were poor.

examples.ko: 장사가 부진한 가게는 문을 닫기도 해요.
examples.en: Shops with weak business sometimes close down.
Exports are sluggish, so the company is very worried.
The team that had been struggling suddenly started winning.

examples.ko: 공부 성적이 부진하면 어떻게 해야 해요?
examples.en: What should I do if my grades are poor?

explain: 성적, 판매, 경기처럼 결과가 기대보다 계속 안 좋을 때 써요. 몸 상태가 나쁠 때는 쓰지 않고 '컨디션이 안 좋다'라고 해요. '저조하다'도 비슷하지만 수치가 낮다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Use it when results such as grades, sales, or game performance stay below expectations. It is not for physical condition; for that say 컨디션이 안 좋다. 저조하다 is similar but focuses more on low numbers.

examples.en: I owe my friend five hundred thousand won.
I owe you for your kindness, so I will repay you someday.

examples.ko: 카드로 계속 쓰다 보면 빚지게 돼요.
examples.en: If you keep spending on a card, you end up in debt.
I don't like owing other people.

examples.ko: 그 사람에게 빚진 마음이 커서 연락하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: I feel so indebted to that person that it's hard to contact them.

examples.ko: 빚지고 사는 것보다 아끼며 사는 게 마음 편해요.
examples.en: Living frugally is more comfortable than living in debt.

explain: '빌리다'는 그냥 빌려 쓰는 것이고, '빚지다'는 갚아야 하는 부담이 남는 느낌이에요. 돈뿐 아니라 은혜나 도움에도 써서 '신세를 지다'와 비슷하게 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: '빌리다' simply means to borrow, while '빚지다' leaves a feeling of an obligation to repay. It is used not only for money but also for favors and help, similar to '신세를 지다'.

examples.ko: 아이를 키우는 데 양육비가 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Raising a child costs a lot.
The government decided to support child-rearing costs.
I am saving up child-rearing money separately every month.

examples.ko: 양육비 부담 때문에 둘째를 망설이는 부부가 많아요.
examples.en: Many couples hesitate to have a second child because of the cost.

examples.ko: 이혼 후에도 부모는 양육비를 나눠 내야 해요.
examples.en: Even after divorce, parents must share the child support.
The child-rearing subsidy is going to increase this year.

explain: 아이를 키우는 데 드는 돈으로, 먹이고 입히고 돌보는 비용을 모두 포함해요. 학교와 학원에 드는 돈은 '교육비'라고 따로 말해요. 뉴스에서는 '양육비 지원', '양육비 부담'이라는 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The money needed to raise a child, covering food, clothes and care. Money for school and extra classes is called 교육비 separately. In the news it appears often as 양육비 지원 or 양육비 부담.

examples.ko: 바자회에서 번 돈으로 봉사단 운영비를 마련하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to raise the volunteer group's operating costs with the money from the bazaar.

examples.ko: 가게 운영비가 매달 너무 많이 들어요.
examples.en: The shop's running costs are too high every month.

examples.ko: 정부가 작은 단체에 운영비를 지원해 줘요.
examples.en: The government supports small organizations with operating costs.
We moved the office to cut operating costs.
Most of the club fees are spent on operating costs.
Operating costs include electricity bills and salaries.

explain: 가게, 학교, 단체를 계속 이어 가는 데 드는 돈이에요. '운영비를 마련하다', '운영비를 지원하다', '운영비를 줄이다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the money needed to keep a shop, school or group running. People commonly say '운영비를 마련하다' (raise), '운영비를 지원하다' (support) and '운영비를 줄이다' (cut).

examples.en: You can deposit and withdraw freely with this account.
I checked my transaction history in the app.

examples.ko: 입출금 통장을 하나 새로 만들고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to open a new checking account.

examples.ko: 입출금 수수료가 무료인 은행을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a bank with no deposit or withdrawal fees.

examples.ko: 은행 점검 시간에는 입출금이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Deposits and withdrawals aren't possible during the bank's maintenance time.
Deposit and withdrawal alert texts keep coming.

explain: 은행에서 '입출금 통장'이라는 말로 가장 많이 만나요. 돈을 넣는 것이 '입금', 빼는 것이 '출금'이고, 둘을 합친 말이에요. ATM이나 앱 화면에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You will meet it most often in '입출금 통장' (an everyday account) at a bank. Putting money in is '입금' and taking it out is '출금', and this word combines them. It also appears often on ATM and app screens.
